name: oxy-f5912345-blind30-ots
instr:
# oxy: thirty one-line faults in an HTTP middleware toolkit, diagnosed without a test suite

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits. What follows is everything that has been observed from the outside.

This library is used to stand a programmable gateway in front of a pool of backend servers: it decides which backend a request goes to, how much traffic a caller is allowed, what happens when a backend is sick, and what gets written down about each exchange. It now gets all of that wrong in a number of places. Nothing about the protocol changed and nothing about the callers changed, yet requests that used to be served are refused, allowances are ignored, and the records kept afterwards do not match what happened.

Standing the thing up, before any traffic flows, is where the trouble starts. A rule saying a request may be replayed onto another backend, written as text asking for a network failure together with an attempt count below a small limit, is turned away the moment it is attached to the proxy even though it is well formed; the same text is turned away again when it is turned into a decision procedure; and an at-most comparison inside such a rule is refused on its own account, so no phrasing of it survives setup. The guard that stops sending traffic to a failing upstream cannot be created at all when its trip rule contains an at-least comparison, construction coming back with an error, while the same rule written with a plain greater-than builds withou
